newsitem.title: FRANCE: SERBIA OPPOSITION READY TO END DEMOS IF LAW VOTED.
newsitem.headline: SERBIA OPPOSITION READY TO END DEMOS IF LAW VOTED.

text.p: Serbian opposition leaders said on Thursday they would end street protests against President Slobodan Milosevic if parliament next Tuesday approved a bill reinstating their municipal election victories in 14 cities.

"We will stop the demonstrations and will give a chance to dialogue" if parliament approves the bill, Vuk Draskovic, a leader of the democratic Zajedno coalition, told reporters after meeting French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.

"We must be very very careful. We had very bad experiences of Mr Milosevic in the past," Draskovic said of the hardline Socialist president's sudden decision to reinstate opposition election victories after 78 days of street protests in Belgrade.

On a brief visit to Paris, Draskovic said all three leaders of Zajedno (Together) agreed to give a chance to talks on other issues such as freeing the media from state control and establishing the independence of the judiciary.

De Charette said Serbia's problems should be resolved by recognition of the election results, dialogue between the government and the opposition, democratic elections as planned by the end of this year and free access to the media.

In a policy switch, France invited the three opposition leaders to Paris after Serbian police used violence against peaceful demonstrators earlier this week, saying the invitation amounted to recognition of the coalition.
